headline.line: The researchers developed a method to estimate pedestrian volumes using push-button traffic signal data, validated against 2,679 hours of video recording 41,843 crosswalk users across 64 signalized intersections in Oregon during Summer 2022.

synthesis.paragraph: In today's research, "What factors drive the vitality of rail transit station areas? An investigation of urban features in Tianjin, China" shares 4 references with the June 23 paper "Beyond single-element thresholds: Statistical compensatory effects among built environment factors in enhancing street vitality", including "Nonlinear and synergistic effects of TOD on urban vibrancy", "Spatial social interaction", and "Street vitality and built environment features". The Tianjin rail transit paper also shares 3 references with the June 14 paper "From global typologies to place-based indicators: An applied geographical approach to TOD in Ho Chi Minh city", including "Travel demand and the 3Ds", "Transit-oriented development (TOD) typologies around metro station areas in urban China", and "Nonlinear and synergistic effects of TOD on urban vibrancy". Additionally, "Fiscally regressive subsidies and the spatial diffusion of electric vehicles in French cities" shares 4 references with the June 22 paper "The impact of purchase subsidy termination on electric vehicle adoption: a synthetic control approach", including "The effectiveness of financial purchase incentives for battery electric vehicles", "An empirical assessment of the impact of subsidies on EV adoption in China", and "Effectiveness and Heterogeneous Effects of Purchase Grants for Electric Vehicles". Among institutional affiliations, Technical University of Munich, University College London, and Peking University each appear on 2 of today's papers.
